**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 91, verses 7–8:**

﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا﴾ He made its creation balanced (ʿadala khalqahā) and perfected its limbs (sawwā aʿḍāʾahā). ʿAṭāʾ said: He means everything He created of jinn and humankind.

﴿فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas, in the transmission of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, said: He made clear to it good and evil. In the transmission of ʿAṭiyya, he said: He taught it obedience and disobedience. al-Kalbī narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from him: He made it know what good it would do and what evil it would guard against [from evil] [[Omitted in "A".]].

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He compelled it to its wickedness and its God-consciousness. Ibn Zayd said: He placed that within it, meaning by His granting it success (tawfīq) toward God-consciousness and His abandonment (khidhlān) of it toward wickedness. al-Zajjāj chose this view and understood the inspiration (ilhām) as success and abandonment. This shows that Allah, mighty and majestic, created God-consciousness in the believer and wickedness in the disbeliever.

Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Shurayḥī informed us: I [Aḥmad ibn] [[Omitted in "A".]] Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Thaʿlabī informed us; al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me; Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh told us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Sufyān informed us; Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm told us; ʿUrwa ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī informed us; Yaḥyā ibn ʿUqayl told us, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur, from al-Aswad al-Dīlī, who said: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said to me: Have you considered what people do and strive for: is it something decreed upon them and carried out among them from a predetermined decree (qadar sabaqa), or is it in what they face from what their Prophet brought them, and the proof (ḥujja) has been established against them? I said: Rather, it is something already decreed upon them. He said: Would that be injustice? I was greatly alarmed by this and said: There is nothing but that it is His creation and His possession; He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned. He said to me: May Allah keep you upright. I only asked you to test your understanding. [A man from Juhayna or Muzayna] [[In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: two men from Muzayna.]] came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, have you considered what people do and strive for: is it something decreed upon them and carried out among them from a predetermined decree, or is it in what they face from what their Prophet brought them, and by which the proof has been established against them? He said: "No, rather it is something already decreed upon them and carried out among them." I said: Then what is the point of action? He said: "Whoever Allah has created for one of the two abodes, Allah will facilitate him toward it. The confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And the soul and He who proportioned it, then inspired it with its wickedness and its God-consciousness﴾." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Qadar, chapter on the manner of the creation of a human in his mother's womb, and the recording of his provision, his term, his deeds, and his wretchedness and felicity, no. (2650), 2/2040–2041.]]

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī informed us; Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Shurayḥ informed us; Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Baghawī informed us; ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd told us; Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya told us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, who said: Surāqa ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum came and said: O Messenger of Allah, make our religion clear to us as if we were created now. Have you considered this ʿumra of ours: is it for this year or forever? He said: "Rather, forever." He said: O Messenger of Allah, make our religion clear to us as if we were created now. What is the point of action today: is it in what the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run with, or is it in what is yet to come? He said: "No, rather in what the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run with." He said: Then what is the point of action? Zuhayr said: He said a word that was hidden from me, so I later asked about it, and it was reported that he heard it. Then he said: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Qadar, chapter on the manner of the creation of a human in his mother's womb, no. (2648), 4/2040–2041.]]

﴿Truly has succeeded he who purifies it﴾. This is the place of the oath. That is, the soul has prospered and been made happy, the soul that Allah has purified (*zakkaha*), meaning He has set it right, cleansed it of sins, and granted it success in obedience.

﴿And truly has failed he who corrupts it﴾. That is, the soul has failed and lost, the soul that Allah has misguided, so that He corrupted it.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is, "Truly has succeeded he who purifies his soul, sets it right, and guides it to the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And truly has failed he who corrupts it," meaning he destroys it, misguides it, and drives it toward disobedience. Thus he attributed the action to the soul.

The word *dassaha* is originally *dassasaha*, from *al-tadsis*, which means concealing something. The second *sin* was changed to a *ya'*. The meaning here is: he humbled it (*akhmalaha*) and hid its station through disbelief and disobedience.

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni narrated to us; Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shurayk al-Shafi'i narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jawrabadhi narrated to us; Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to us; Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Uthman and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I will not say to you except what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, senility, and the punishment of the grave. O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it; You are its Guardian and its Master. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a soul that is never satisfied, from a heart that does not humble itself, and from a supplication that is not answered.'"

[[Reported by Muslim in al-Dhikr wal-Du'a wal-Tawba wal-Istighfar, chapter on seeking refuge from the evil of what one has done and the evil of what one has not done, no. 2722: 4/2088; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 5/158–159.]]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni narrated to us; Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shurayk al-Shafi'i narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jawrabadhi narrated to us; Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to us; Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Uthman and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I will not say to you except what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, senility, and the punishment of the grave. O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it; You are its Guardian and its Master. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a soul that is never satisfied, from a heart that does not humble itself, and from a supplication that is not answered.'"

[[Reported by Muslim in al-Dhikr wal-Du'a wal-Tawba wal-Istighfar, chapter on seeking refuge from the evil of what one has done and the evil of what one has not done, no. 2722: 4/2088; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 5/158–159.]]

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Thamud denied through their transgression﴾, meaning through their rebellion and their aggression; that is, rebellion led them to deny.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 91, verses 12–15:**

﴿When the most wretched of them set out﴾, meaning he stood up. *Al-inbi'ath* (setting out) is hastening to obey the one who sends forth, i.e., they denied the punishment and denied Salih when the most wretched of them set out. He was Qudar ibn Salif, who was reddish-haired, blue-eyed, [the eyes] [[Omitted from "A".]] and short, and he stood up to hamstring the she-camel.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il [Musa ibn Isma'il informed us] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]], narrated to us Wuhayb, narrated to us Hisham from his father, that Abd Allah ibn Zam'a informed him that he heard the Prophet ﷺ delivering a sermon, and he mentioned the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her, and said [the Messenger of Allah ﷺ]: [[Omitted from "A".]] "When the most wretched of them set out" – a mighty, [ʿārim] [[That is, the wicked, corrupt, and vile one; it is also said: the strong and fierce one.]] man set out for her, stalwart among his people, like Abu Zam'a." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir Surat al-Shams: 8/705, and by Muslim in al-Jannah, Sifat Na'imiha wa Ahliha, no. (2855): 4/2191.]]

﴿The Messenger of Allah said to them﴾, Salih, peace be upon him, ﴿"the she-camel of Allah"﴾, meaning beware of hamstringing the she-camel of Allah. Al-Zajjaj said: it is in the accusative on the sense of "leave the she-camel of Allah", ﴿and her drink﴾, her share of water; i.e., leave the she-camel of Allah and leave her share of the water, [so do not obstruct] [[In "B": fa-la ta'taridu, "do not obstruct."]] the water on the day of her drinking.

﴿But they denied him﴾, meaning Salih, ﴿and hamstrung her﴾, meaning the she-camel.

﴿So their Lord crushed them﴾. Ata and Muqatil said: their Lord destroyed them and annihilated them. Al-Mu'arrij said: *al-damdama* is destruction by total annihilation.

﴿for their sin﴾, by their denial of the Messenger and their hamstringing of the she-camel. ﴿And He leveled it﴾, He leveled the destruction upon them all, encompassing them with it so that not one of them escaped. Al-Farra' said: He leveled the community and sent the punishment upon its young and its old, meaning He made them equal.

﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾. The people of Medina and Syria recited *"fa-la"* with the *fa'* (so), and it is so in their codices. The rest recited with the *waw* (and), and it is so in their codices too. ﴿Its consequence﴾ means its outcome.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah does not fear any retribution from anyone for destroying them. This is the narration of Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Kalbi said: it refers back to the one who hamstrung her, and there is inversion and deferral in the speech, and its estimated sense is: "When the most wretched of them set out, and He does not fear its consequence."
